Phase 1 RCA (confirmed before repair): `tests/conftest.py::_remove_readonly_run_snapshots` materializes `tuple(tmp_path.rglob(".rebar/run_snapshots"))`, so it recursively enters every unrelated mutable subtree below a test temp root, including `tests/interfaces/conftest.py::rebar_repo`'s live `repo/.tickets-tracker`. The canonical store write lifecycle intentionally creates and removes `.ticket-write.lock.d` (`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` dual-window contract). Python 3.11 `Path.rglob` caches directory entries from a parent scan and catches `PermissionError` but not `FileNotFoundError` when a cached child vanishes before descent; Python 3.12+ delegates to a walk that ignores the same scandir error. A deterministic runtime barrier used the real `rebar._store.lock.acquire`: after the tracker parent scan cached the live mkdir lock, `LockHandle.release()` removed it; the actual fixture teardown then raised the exact `FileNotFoundError` at `.ticket-write.lock.d` on Python 3.11. The identical barrier returned normally on Python 3.12. This proves canonical lock churn plus the broad mutation-intolerant scan and supported 3.11 traversal semantics are sufficient, while a stable tree or 3.11 alone is not.

The competing hypothesis that MCP async completion or the lock lifecycle is defective was rejected. Under a real held lock, direct cleanup of an exact `.rebar/run_snapshots` root succeeded and left the lock intact; only the fixture's broad traversal failed when release occurred mid-walk. Async daemon execution and dual-window lock removal are explicit contracts (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`). Fixture ordering is not causal: direct invocation of the actual fixture reproduced outside pytest fixture scheduling.

Defect legitimacy: Python 3.11 is an explicit supported CI/runtime target (`.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`, `pyproject.toml`), and closed bug `actinium-civic-needletail` requires shared cleanup of every exact `.rebar/run_snapshots` below test-owned `tmp_path` while preserving unrelated content and read-only publication. Commit `bedfb276...` introduced this regression. Expected repair behavior: retain recursive exact-root coverage and tolerate only unrelated entries that disappear concurrently; do not change workflow async semantics, store locking, snapshot permissions, or mask non-disappearance filesystem errors.
